name: Torval
description: Hold Shift and hover any word (Japanese, Italian or Spanish) to see what it means.
author: Jacob Gerritz
_comment_id: Deliberately still says lll. This is not a name, it is the key Firefox
files the add-on's storage under, and the known and ignored word lists
live in that storage. Renaming it would not rename anything a reader
sees; it would hand the add-on a different, empty drawer and leave
however many months of reading in the old one, unreachable. Change it
only together with exporting the word lists first and importing them

_comment_min_version: 128, not 140, on purpose. Marking the unknown words on a page uses
an API that arrived in 140 and is simply skipped without it, so a
reader on 128 still gets the dictionary, the reader, the subtitles
and Anki. The store's linter warns that 128 predates
data_collection_permissions below; older Firefox ignores that key
rather than choking on it, and losing twelve versions of Firefox to
silence a warning about a field they cannot read would be a poor
_comment_data: Torval collects nothing. Everything it knows stays in this browser:
the dictionaries in IndexedDB, the word lists in extension storage,
the Anki settings likewise. It talks to exactly three places, all of
them at the user's own instruction: AnkiConnect on localhost, the
video site being watched, and the audio host for a word's
pronunciation. Saying so here is what the add-on store asks for, and
it is checked against the permissions above.
